text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Civil servants get 2.8 pct wage increase this year. (p1)
- Plastics processor Wavin is re-thinking its current shareholder structure. (p1)
- Introduction of the European single currency will cost Dutch businesses some five billion guilders. (p1)
- Audio and multimedia CD producer Docdata is returning to the Amsterdam Stock Exchange after four years. (p1)
- Travel Unie Internationaal Nederland sees 1996 net fall by 70 pct to Dfl 9.4 million due to costs of merger. (p3)
- Accountancy and consultancy group KPMG books 12 pct higher turnover mainly through consultancy sector. (p3)
- Dutch transport organisation KNV presses European Commission to compensate for damages from truckers strikes. (p3)
- Engineering concern Stork takes over traffic management systems companies Marine Solair and Traffitec Holland. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Drop in long-term unemployed continues according to central statistics office CBS. (p1)
- Cows at farm where first Dutch mad cow disease case was found are free of BSE. (p1)
- High-tech companies most popular in first quarter on Amsterdam Stock Exchange with 40 pct price increase. (p33)
- Revolving fund to support Dutch aerospace sector is empty. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Employees can put aside part of their wages free of taxation to save up for half a year of sabbatical leave. (p1)
- The Netherlands, Portugal and Greece are among the few ecomomic growth countries of the European Union. (p33)
- Builder HBG gets three representatives in the board of its German acquistion Wayss & Freitag. (p33)
- PM Wim Kok says in Germany's weekly 'Die Zeit' EMU criteria are more important than time scheme. (p35)
- Employers association VNO-NCW chairman thinks environmental target for decreasing emission of green house gases is too ambitious. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch cabinet should diminish budgetary deficit instead of reducing the tax burden next year according to the IMF. (p1)
- Rabobank talks with European union of cooperative banks Unico about forms of cooperation on the capital markets. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
